$comment: Open-modules ↔ process map (founder 2026-10-02, deepened same day): which lib/openstartup modules serve which corpus processes, and — in steps — which module FUNCTION genuinely computes which step's math. Keyed by module id (the lib/openstartup file basename); label/anchor mirror the module's heading in open-modules/README.md (anchor = GitHub's heading slug — process pages link there, repo-first, no new site pages); processes = corpus.json task ids the module honestly serves, grounded in the corpus text (83(b) appears in form_001/startup_002/form_012; the franchise-tax math serves tax_001 and the sit_010 delinquency cure; …). steps entries are {processId, nodeId, module, function, what}: curated from BOTH sides (the module's real exports and the corpus step text), and only where the named function computes that step's math — no decorating; steps a module merely informs stay task-level. Every step's (module, processId) pair must also appear in that module's processes list. Modules with no honest process target would simply be absent — nothing is forced. Read back by lib/businessLogicMap.ts (chips: process pages' 'Open modules' line at task level, per-step 'compute:' chips in ProcessDag); the Serves lines in open-modules/README.md are generated from this file (scripts/generate-business-logic-serves.ts). Totality-tested both ways (module file exists, process id exists, node id exists in that process's DAG, the named export IS a function, anchors match README headings, README Serves lines in sync) in lib/__tests__/businessLogicMap.test.ts + businessLogicServes.test.ts.
